cite.claim: Encyclopaedia Judaica (JVL): Haganah took Haifa 21-22 April 1948; this account attributes the Arab departure to Arab High Command orders
cite.quote: In a lightning military action, the Haganah captured the Arab quarters and took over the city. Only about 3,000 of Haifa’s 50,000 Arab residents chose to remain in the city; the rest, in response to the Arab High Command’s orders, refused to accept Jewish rule and abandoned their homes.

cite.claim: Late 1948 population 97,544, 96% Jewish
cite.quote: Late in 1948, Haifa’s population numbered 97,544, of whom 96% were Jews.

status_cites.note: Taken by the Haganah on 21-22 April 1948, before the declaration of independence. Sources agree most of the Arab population left; they differ on why (PalQuest: the attacks prompted a mass exodus; Encyclopaedia Judaica/JVL: Arab High Command orders to leave).
